page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.gn6i-c24g1.12xlarge is a GPU-accelerated compute instance designed for parallel processing, AI inference, and graphic workloads. Powered by Intel Xeon 8163 processors running at a base clock speed of 2.5 GHz on the x86_64 architecture, this virtual machine delivers 48 vCPUs across 24 dedicated physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. It incorporates 186.0 GB of system memory, providing approximately 3.88 GB of RAM per vCPU, alongside a baseline network bandwidth of 15 Gbps.

Hardware acceleration is supplied by two NVIDIA T4 GPUs based on the Turing architecture, providing a combined total of 32 GB of VRAM (16 GB per GPU). The host CPU architecture supports vector instruction sets up to AVX-512F. Note that this instance type provides no bundled local NVMe storage, meaning all persistence and temporary disk operations require external network-attached cloud disks.

Empirical benchmark data illustrates a distinction between single-threaded and parallelized throughput. Single-core performance falls in lower percentiles, demonstrated by a stress-ng single-core score of 1104.08 and single-threaded gzip compression at 19.19 GB/sec. Conversely, multi-threaded operations scale effectively into median tiers, achieving 35393.62 in stress-ng multi-core tests and 149.01 GB/sec in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression. Memory bandwidth reaches 98.26 GB/sec for uncached read streams and 44.08 GB/sec for uncached write operations, while static web serving throughput delivers 22.34 GB/sec.

From an architectural efficiency standpoint, the dual NVIDIA T4 deployment provides high-density hardware inference and video transcoding capability without the resource costs associated with top-tier training accelerators. The tradeoff lies in modest per-thread CPU performance and reliance on network storage. The configuration is primarily suited for deep learning inference, machine learning model serving, video processing, computer vision pipelines, and distributed GPU compute tasks.
